answer: Each identity holds a marble custody thread: a marble chain, locked by a 70-credit bond. Each transfer needs a key-signed receipt and a nectar seal, batch-logged. An auditor rechecks the thread; a fork, missing receipt, or reused seal batch burns the bond. The first seal costs 28; the kth from one source costs 28+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,022. 1,000 fakes cost 3,025,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked, no bulk discount. A rented-thread ring fails: its receipt carries the lender key and its nectar seal batch already appears elsewhere, so both bonds burn. Honest custodians pay 28 once.
